points: The Oct 18 print will report the already-closed Q1 FY2027 quarter and update FY27 guidance, revealing whether the June in-line outlook is tracking or needs revision.

Reports from the June 24 Q4 FY2026 release suggest Paychex delivered strong double-digit revenue and earnings growth and issued an in-line FY27 outlook; the next print shows whether that momentum carried into Q1.
Consensus expects FY1 EPS of $5.98, up 8.5%, and FY2 EPS of $6.39, up 6.8%; the print's guidance language will show if the path to those numbers is intact or at risk.

The 90-day revenue estimate is up 1.33% and the last 30 days show 2 upward analyst revisions versus 1 downward; the print will reveal whether that modest optimism is justified by actual Q1 performance.

Valuation is flagged as fair at roughly 21.2x FY1 P/E and a PEG near 2.5 versus the theme median; the long case depends on the print confirming stable enough growth to keep that valuation fair, not cheap.

Peer prints from FA, RHI, and UPWK in early November follow a few weeks later; Paychex's read-through on employment-services demand and small-business payroll trends will set the tone for how those reports are judged.

The following quarters set up as a guidance story: if FY27 guidance is held or raised, the 6.8% FY2 growth and fair multiple give the long a fundamental floor, while a guidance cut would leave the PEG near 2.5 with little room for error.
watch: Q1 FY2027 revenue and EPS versus pre-print consensus and any FY27 guidance revision — a beat or raise supports the long, a miss or cut undermines it.
FY1 EPS estimate of $5.98 and FY2 EPS estimate of $6.39 — guidance that preserves the 8.5% and 6.8% growth path supports the long.
90-day revenue estimate revision of +1.33% and 30-day analyst up/down of 2/1 — continued upward estimate momentum supports the long.
P/E near 21.2x and PEG near 2.5 versus the theme median fair — a stable or improving growth outlook keeps valuation fair and supports the long.
